status.comment: requires a real Linux or macOS host

p.PURPOSE: Prove that the package's `posix` profile publishes the exact Bash launcher as executable `$VIBE_SETTINGS/opt/bin/claudez` (production default: `~/.vibe/opt/bin/claudez`), without changing PATH or copying credentials, and that its process contract preserves cwd, argv and exit.

step-deploy.title: Step 1 — deploy into an isolated settings root

p.EXPECTED-DEPLOY: Expected: exit 0; exactly one launcher exists at `$VIBE_SETTINGS/opt/bin/claudez`; its SHA-256 equals the installed package's `launchers/claudez`; its permission mode is exactly `0755`; deployment state owns that file and no token file exists under the isolated settings root.

p.STEP-CONTRACT: Put a fake `claude` first on a scratch PATH and point `ZAI_API_TOKEN_FILE` at a non-secret fixture. The fake executable checks the expected provider/model/state variables without printing the bearer, records cwd and argv, and exits 37. Invoke the deployed launcher from a different cwd with arguments containing spaces.

p.EXPECTED-CONTRACT: Expected: launcher exit 37; recorded cwd equals the caller's cwd; argv is byte-for-byte the supplied sequence; provider/model/state checks pass; stdout/stderr contain no fixture bearer; no file outside scratch changes.

p.EXPECTED-INVERSE: Expected: unchanged receipt-owned launcher is removed and neighbors remain. Repeating after redeploy with mode changed from `0755` refuses or enters the specified recovery path; it never reports content-only freshness.

p.PASS: All three steps match their expected paragraphs and a human signs off the real host behavior.
